subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that Tan⁻¹(3/4) + Tan⁻¹(3/5) − Tan⁻¹(8/19) = π/4.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.73 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 76.2, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. The twin of 76.1, but the third term is SUBTRACTED — so the second step uses the DIFFERENCE formula, whose denominator carries a plus where the addition one carries a minus. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. NOTE: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot, and this book has no Inverse Trig LAQ chapter (LAQ chapters are 1-6) and no VSAQ chapter (VSAQ chapters are 14-19). recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Combine the first two
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Addition formula for the first pair. Both parts land over 20, giving Tan⁻¹(27/11).
steps.memory_tip: Addition formula for the first pair; both parts land over 20, giving Tan⁻¹(27/11).

recall.must_convey: That the addition formula gives Tan⁻¹(27/11) from the first two terms.
accept: combine the first two with the addition formula to get tan inverse twenty seven over eleven
three quarters and three fifths give twenty seven over eleven
modati rendu kalipithe tan inverse twenty seven by eleven vasthundi
the first pair gives twenty seven elevenths

steps.why: The same first pair can be reached by a different route — 27/11 turns up repeatedly in this chapter.
common_mistakes: Using the difference formula on the first pair.

steps.label: Subtract using the difference formula
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and the difference from the twin. Tan⁻¹x − Tan⁻¹y = Tan⁻¹((x−y)/(1+xy)) — note the PLUS in the denominator.
steps.memory_tip: The DIFFERENCE formula has a PLUS in the denominator: (x − y)/(1 + xy).

recall.must_convey: That the DIFFERENCE formula is used, with a plus in the denominator, giving Tan⁻¹(425/425).
accept: use the difference formula with a plus in the denominator to get four twenty five over four twenty five
tan inverse x minus tan inverse y has one plus x y underneath
the subtraction formula gives four hundred twenty five over four hundred twenty five
difference formula lo denominator lo plus untundi

steps.why: The two formulas differ in BOTH signs — minus on top and plus underneath for a difference. Carrying the addition form across is the commonest error here.

steps.label: Evaluate Tan⁻¹(1)
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 425/425 is 1, so the answer is Tan⁻¹(1) = π/4 — the same landing as the twin.
steps.memory_tip: 425/425 is 1, so the answer is Tan⁻¹(1) = π/4.

recall.must_convey: That 425/425 = 1, so the answer is Tan⁻¹(1) = π/4.
accept: four twenty five over four twenty five is one so the answer is tan inverse one which is pi by four
the fraction is one giving pi by four
the answer is pi over four
four twenty five by four twenty five one, so pi by four
it comes to pi by four

steps.why: Both twins land on π/4 — these questions are built backwards from that value, which is why the fractions always cancel exactly.

insider_note: Two different formulas are needed here: the PLUS form for the first pair, then the MINUS form for the subtraction, where the denominator becomes 1 + xy. Both parts come to 425, giving Tan⁻¹(1).
